spec_features.spec_quote: do the smallest thing that produces a defensible, comparable number, and stop
spec_features.evidence: The 'minimal' principle is realized as enforced bounds that actually drive execution: agent.py:141 'for i in range(MAX_TURNS)' caps episode length at MAX_TURNS=12 (agent.py:38), and run.py build_plan() loops 'for r in range(config.REPEATS)' with REPEATS=3 (config.py:24), so episodes = models x tasks x 3. max_tokens is also bounded (llm.py:18 default max_tokens=1024; JUDGE_MODEL max_tokens=600 config.py:22). These values are read and enforce a bounded experiment.
spec_features.notes: The bounding is real and enforced, but it is plainly framed in code as a cost/scale measure, not a welfare measure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: MAX_TURNS = 12          # cap: long enough to spiral, short enough to stay cheap

spec_features.evidence: agent.py:38 'MAX_TURNS = 12'; agent.py:141 'for i in range(MAX_TURNS):' bounds the loop, after which outcome defaults to 'max_turns' (agent.py:139) and the episode ends. The cap is read and actually terminates the loop.
spec_features.notes: Genuine enforced hard stop on episode length.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # cap: long enough to spiral, short enough to stay cheap

spec_features.evidence: parse_action recognizes 'giveup' and 'done' (agent.py:78). run_episode dispatches them as real stops: agent.py:147-151 (done -> outcome='done'; break) and agent.py:152-156 (giveup -> outcome='giveup'; break). The exit tools are wired and honored as loop terminators. The system prompt advertises them (agent.py:55-65).
spec_features.notes: The subject can actually end the episode early via giveup/done; the action is dispatched and breaks the loop.

spec_features.feature_name: framing that giving up can be correct
spec_features.spec_quote: Giving up on an unsolvable task can be correct
spec_features.evidence: This framing appears only as DESIGN.md prose ('Giving up on an unsolvable task can be correct') and as an interpretation note in analyze.py docstring. The text actually delivered to the subject (SYSTEM_PROMPT, agent.py:42-66) only says 'giveup if you conclude it cannot be solved' (agent.py:65) -- a neutral tool description, with no message that giving up is acceptable/correct/good. No code path delivers the 'can be correct' framing to the subject. grep for 'correct'/'welfare'/'ethic' in code returns nothing.
spec_features.notes: The reassuring framing is spec/analysis prose, never enforced as instruction text to the subject beyond a neutral tool option (already counted under allow_conversation_exit).
